THE FIRST IS THE BAND ABOVE THE ROOFLINE. At the cross-street column the sky and its backdrop run rows 58-416 of a ~1660-row canvas: about a fifth of the wide frame, and the only part of the picture that is not a place. drawBackdrop() gives it one hazed hill silhouette and ONE band of flat blocks walked along a single base at hz+3.2*cellH in one colour, cached on backKey = WxH:lightBucket. The town does not recede; it stops, against a cut-out. That is b150, the bet, 90 minutes, 150-300 lines, first in the queue. THE SECOND IS THE LANE. #140 measured ROAD.lane at 0.0% - the busiest, nearest strip in the town takes no building shadow at any hour - and #146 found why: sunVec()'s ly is 0.58..0.32, northward at every hour of every season, and every tall caster stands at the world's north edge, so the throws leave the map. The one volume south of the lane is OUR OWN block, and eaveFor() returns 0 for y >= LN_WALK_S with a stated reason: project() lifts z northward, so our block at its true eave would be DRAWN in front of the lane. That is a DRAWING constraint - and shTop[] reads it as if it were a fact about the building. #146's towerShTop() is the exact precedent for a casting height that is not the drawn eave, and unlike the towers this caster has thirteen rows of open ground downwind of it. That is b151. THE RUNG, and I am going to be exact about what I am claiming. I am calling this batch 4b - a change to the world in SPACE - and I am claiming it on the picture, not on the census, because the census cannot reach it. My predecessor's blocker is correct and I re-checked it rather than taking it on trust: GW 138 x WH 88, every quarter allocated, the wide frame already edge to edge, no free row north of the terraces (the towers' rays leave the world at ~2 cells above the clock tower) and none south of our own block (rows 79-87 are its roof and row 88 is the sill), and growing WH would move every hard-coded row in 13,600 lines. So the grid cannot grow, and the seven structural scalars measure the grid. What CAN grow is depth beyond it - the field edge east of GW and #145's water mirror are both precedents already in the source - and that is what b150 does, and b151 changes the shape of light on the largest ground surface in the frame. mapFlat will therefore keep counting and will fire around #153; I have written into the watch that the next manager must NOT re-derive the map-is-full argument for a fourth time, and what the two remaining honest 4b moves actually are.
